engagement_background.objective: Identify and realize $0.7-1.4 million in annual cost savings across key spend categories and lay the foundation for stronger procurement discipline, thereby enhancing Advantia Health’s EBITDA and supporting its PE value-creation plan.
engagement_background.scope_summary: Treya will run strategic sourcing initiatives for 10 spend categories representing roughly $19 million of the company’s $45 million total spend (e.g., employee benefits, medical supplies, medical & diagnostic devices, billing/RCM, telecom, data-center hosting, office supplies). Work includes competitive RFPs, incumbent negotiations, and GPO leverage, plus a review of Advantia’s procure-to-pay processes; employee benefits is an optional later phase and some suppliers may prove non-addressable after deep-dives.
constraints_challenges: Limited strategic procurement resources and focus prior to engagement
Fragmented spend split between two AP/P-card systems (Advantia Mid-Atlantic and Heartland) with incomplete line-item detail
Lack of full back-end integration from recent acquisitions leading to decentralized buying behavior
Need to secure additional usage and contract data directly from suppliers due to poor internal visibility
Tight 4-6-month timeline to deliver savings while minimizing disruption to clinical operations
Incumbent clinical supplier relationships that may resist pricing pressure or vendor changes

procurement_environment.data_availability: Basic AP and P-card spend data are available from two separate systems; contracts and detailed usage must be requested from suppliers.
procurement_environment.data_quality_notes: Multiple naming conventions, sparse item-level detail, and gaps caused by non-responsive suppliers; spend visibility not centralized across acquired practices.
